compatibility.note: Use 0.2.0-preview.12 or a later compatible release for this collection. The portable projects' runtime property bindings, camera capture, photo badges, native tag buttons and multi-schedule/S3 backups require at least preview.11; the setup-required industrial devices workshop requires preview.12. The bundle source revision and each workshop prerequisites identify its actual requirements; exact artifact/source evidence is recorded separately in docs/architecture/PARITY.md.

workshops.title: Visitor check-in and photo badges
workshops.summary: A camera-equipped welcome form renders a visitor badge through Labelary, then resets for the next visitor.
prerequisites: Use preview.11 or a later compatible build containing Computer camera and transient Image URL support. Preview.10 installers do not include these components.
A browser with camera access on HTTPS or localhost, a webcam, and internet access to https://api.labelary.com.
Publish as a gateway administrator and open the operator application with Operate permission, or explicitly enable live actions in Designer Preview.
Use synthetic visitor details while learning: name, email, host and photo are sent to the external Labelary service. No database or tags are required.
walkthrough: Import visitor-checkin.sparkproj from artifacts/sparkproj. On Welcome select visitor-controller in Layers; General shows its component ID, and Actions & Events → Messages contains check-in and dismiss handlers. Create badge's Send message action lists its matching receiver.
Publish the application and open its operator link. Enter a synthetic name and email, then choose a host.
Click Start camera, allow browser camera access, then Capture photo. Retake if needed. Camera access begins only after the visitor clicks Start camera.
Click Create badge. A PNG label from Labelary replaces the form and includes the visitor’s captured photo.
Click Dismiss. The badge and all local visitor values clear and the blank Welcome form returns. Start camera again for the next visitor.
Try an empty form or disconnect the internet: validation/error messages keep the form available, with no automatic retry or duplicate requests.

workshops.title: Runtime property bindings
workshops.summary: Live chart settings, bound custom values, typed datasets and reusable layout bindings.
prerequisites: Requires preview.11 or a later compatible build with runtime property bindings; preview.10 does not include this feature.
Import, review and explicitly publish. No tags, connections, Python scripts or equipment writes are required.
walkthrough: Change Chart maximum and confirm the chart axis follows its bound custom property.
Toggle Show chart legend: the legend, table row count and repeater columns change.
Change Repeater gap and Split position. The bound split handle is controlled by its source.
Write different notes in each form and change layout settings; unrelated note values remain independent.
Open a second operator tab and verify its session starts with independent defaults.
In Designer inspect fx on chart, dataset, split and repeater rows; inspect the bound custom property at the bottom.

workshops.title: Alarms and retained history
workshops.summary: Synthetic temperature alarms, selected-rule configuration, acknowledgement, persistent journal and historical trend.
features: Separate Alarms and History lists with selected-rule property forms
Searchable configured tag browser for alarm and history paths
prerequisites: Use preview.11 or a later compatible build for the selected-rule Alarms/History editors and browsable tag paths. Preview.10 includes the earlier local alarms/history implementation.
Run tools/load-process-data-example.mjs against an isolated gateway using administrator credentials; --publish is explicit.
Operators need View to read, Commands to change the synthetic temperature and Operate to acknowledge; tag scope must include [default]ProcessWorkshop/.
walkthrough: In Gateway Settings > Alarms, select the high-temperature rule, inspect Browse beside Tag path and stage a deadband change. Switch to History, select the workshop tag and stage a retention change; Cancel changes restores both tabs without saving.
Publish and open the workshop. Review and confirm 90 as the synthetic temperature, then acknowledge the high alarm.
Set 78 and confirm the alarm remains active; set 74 and confirm it clears.
Set 10 to activate low, then 23 to clear. Compare journal events and historical values in two operator tabs.
Restart only the isolated gateway and verify retained alarm occurrence, acknowledgement and history.
Remove the workshop project and disable its alarm/history rules when finished; no physical equipment was used.

workshops.title: Retained view containers
workshops.summary: Reusable forms in embedded, tab, split and dock layouts with independent retained pane state.
prerequisites: Use preview.10 or later compatible release.
Import the package, review and explicitly publish. Synthetic form actions and events require Operate permission and the bundled Python runtime. No connections or tags are needed.
walkthrough: In Designer, select the container, open View container → Edit panes, and inspect each pane's shared template and parameter overrides. Edit the form itself under Project → Templates.
Edit a form in one tab, switch tabs and return to verify its draft is retained.
Use arrow keys, Home and End on the tab strip to navigate.
Open the split screen and resize with the pointer and keyboard.
Hide and reopen a dock to verify its private values remain.
Run a pane action and open its contextual popup; compare another pane and another operator tab.

workshops.title: Validated inputs workshop
workshops.summary: Formatted part codes, inline validation and repeat barcode scans with session-local Python feedback.
prerequisites: Use preview.10 or later for these controls.
The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are required.
walkthrough: Enter ab0012 and Tab to format the part as AB-0012.
Enter an invalid email, then operator@example.test, observing inline messages.
Scan 000123 plus Enter twice and confirm both commits while retaining leading zeroes.
Validate an incomplete form, then a complete form. Compare independent state in another operator tab.

workshops.title: Component interaction workshop
workshops.summary: Keyboard, focus and pointer handlers in Python and JavaScript with independent template forms.
prerequisites: Use preview.10 or later for these events.
Python handlers require the bundled runtime and operator Operate permission.
walkthrough: Focus and type into fields, then use arrow keys and Tab to inspect their event details.
Type slowly into the password field and confirm the counter changes without revealing keys.
Press, release and double-click the pad, then compare disabled and hidden behavior.
Compare independent station A and B forms and a second operator tab.

workshops.title: Atomic table batch editing
workshops.summary: Select several synthetic work orders, stage cell changes and save them in one SQLite transaction.
features: Atomic SQLite and SQL Server batch contract
prerequisites: Use the companion application-workflows source build or a later compatible release.
Run tools/load-table-batch-example.mjs on an isolated gateway to create its synthetic SQLite database and project; --publish explicitly publishes.
Operators need Operate permission to apply changes. SQL Server uses the same transaction contract but this workshop exercises SQLite.
walkthrough: Load and explicitly publish the synthetic workshop.
Select multiple rows, open the batch editor and stage changes; Cancel must leave records unchanged.
Apply changes and confirm the affected row versions advance once each.
Use two operator tabs to stage conflicting edits; the losing batch must update no rows.

workshops.title: Access boundaries workshop
workshops.summary: Separate operator commands and delegated gateway capabilities with a synthetic memory-tag application.
prerequisites: Use tools/load-access-permissions-example.mjs on an isolated gateway. It adds one scoped synthetic memory tag.
Create disposable local accounts manually with the profiles in the guide; no credentials are packaged.
walkthrough: Load and publish the workshop on an isolated gateway.
In Security → Operator settings, select the workshop's project tag access entry and verify its narrow multiline prefix; compare another project's draft without granting extra access.
Compare Viewer, Operator and Command operator profiles.
Exercise the five delegated gateway profiles and confirm other operations are denied.
Disable a disposable account and verify its sessions lose access.

workshops.title: Equipment commands workshop
workshops.summary: Reviewed equipment controls and simple fixed/property-sourced tag buttons using synthetic memory tags.
features: Current input and parent-property value sources
prerequisites: Native buttons require preview.11 or a later compatible build containing Set tag value actions; preview.10 does not include them.
Run tools/load-equipment-commands-example.mjs on an isolated gateway; --publish explicitly publishes.
No equipment connection is configured. Non-admin operators need explicit Commands and tag-read access.
walkthrough: Review and confirm a speed, run flag and note.
Cancel a review and reject an out-of-range speed.
Change the target from another session after review; confirm stale requests are rejected.
Compare Operate-only and Commands accounts and inspect audit references.
Open Native tag actions, edit the numeric, Boolean and text fields, then activate their buttons. Confirm the exact reviewed input values.
Use Quick write: 25 and Write parent screen height to change the separate synthetic quick tag without a confirmation dialog.
In Designer inspect Edit actions & events → On click → Set tag value. Choose a fixed value or a component property; Apply is one undo step.

workshops.title: Reusable unit model workshop
workshops.summary: Pinned UDT versions, member overrides and named scan groups using two synthetic counter instances.
prerequisites: Run tools/load-unit-model-example.mjs against an isolated gateway using a local administrator credential file.
Creates six synthetic tags, two instances and one scan group; no OPC connection.
walkthrough: Verify West 50% and East 75%.
Create version 2 and upgrade West through preview, retaining its Goal override.
Observe West 62.5%, then disable and restore the scan group.

workshops.title: Tag-driven template parameters
workshops.summary: Live typed tag parameters resolve a bounded machine address and reconstruct authoritative context for actions.
prerequisites: Create the two independently authored BindingWorkshop/A/Count and B/Count memory Double tags with values 12 and 27.
Configure the operator project readable tag prefix. No physical device is used.
walkthrough: Load the authored tags and screen into a separate project.
Select A or B and verify parameter readings.
Disable the source or change its type to inspect unavailable-state handling.

workshops.title: Datasets and nested query rows
workshops.summary: Named-query datasets and two nested query levels preserve independent form and popup context.
features: Stable row context and private drafts
prerequisites: Use the companion dataset/nested-query source build and bundled Python.
Uses only the built-in production-summary sample connection.
walkthrough: Import, review and publish the project.
Compare both nested row levels and their per-row charts.
Edit independent notes and open row-context popups; verify context after refresh.

workshops.title: Supplied-data charts workshop
workshops.summary: Ten chart modes, quality gaps, configurable axes and local range selection over synthetic datasets.
prerequisites: Use the companion dataset/chart source build. No database, device or Python is required.
walkthrough: Import and publish, then visit Production, Quality and Scheduling.
Adjust the range selector and expand View data.
Edit series/axes in Designer; Apply, Undo, Save and Publish.

workshops.title: Unified application publication
workshops.summary: Review and release screens, queries, libraries and gateway/browser events together; roll back the same complete version.
prerequisites: Use the companion source build with unified publication and bundled Python.
Imported event and library resources are disabled until reviewed and enabled.
walkthrough: Import and enable the three sample resources, then save and publish Amber.
Change the library and query to Indigo and publish the complete application.
Roll back Amber; verify the library, query and events match while drafts retain Indigo.

workshops.title: Lifecycle and session messaging workshop
workshops.summary: Python mount/cleanup, unified action authoring and transient gateway messages across independently identified operator tabs.
features: gateway broadcast and targeted tab messaging
prerequisites: Use the companion SparkStudio 0.2.0-preview.9 release or a newer compatible build, with its bundled Python runtime.
Import then publish the project; sign into two operator tabs with Operate permission.
The optional gateway message script imports disabled and requires separate review, enabling and script publication.
walkthrough: Verify both template receivers show their Python mount text, then broadcast a note to two operator tabs.
Identify the open tabs and send to one explicit session ID; only its receivers change.
Rename a button using self.text, leave the screen and return to fresh mounted receivers.
Populate the message field through Python self.value and confirm the next broadcast uses that value.
Inspect all event families and native actions in one staged Actions & Events dialog.
Check valid and invalid Python syntax without running or saving the edited code, then Cancel.
Optionally enable and publish Workshop broadcast, invoke it with Test published handler, then disable and republish.

workshops.title: Python component events workshop
workshops.summary: Load synthetic work orders, validate quantities and handle local messages with Python input and property events in independent forms.
features: Python input change and commit handlers
Python property-change handlers with previous/current values and origin
typed private state and input bindings
independent template placements and repeated rows
prerequisites: Use the companion SparkStudio 0.2.0-preview.9 release or a newer compatible build, with bundled CPython. Older Python-button-only builds do not support these handlers.
Import, review and explicitly publish the project. Operators need Operate permission; Designer Preview requires an administrator to enable Live actions.
Synthetic records and session drafts require no database, tags, device or internet connection. Local drafts reset on navigation or reload; this example does not persist production records.
walkthrough: Select WO1002 in Station A. The Python commit handler loads Mounting bracket and target 24, while Station B stays on its original order.
Read the property-event line after loading an order. It records the part change and its origin.
Set quantity to 0 or above its target. The Python change handler shows a validation message and disables Store session draft. Correct it and store a local draft.
Edit Operator note and watch its Python change handler update the neighboring label.
Press Reset through message. Its Python receiver resets this form's quantity and local draft only.
Open repeated stations and repeat in Row 1. Compare Row 2 and a second operator browser tab; no local state is shared between them.
Open Actions & Events, compare Python and JavaScript for input, property and message handlers, then export and re-import the authored definitions. Reload restores defaults.

workshops.title: Python UI workshop
workshops.summary: Change local display properties and declared state from published Python button actions; compare independent template rows with an optional shared gateway tag.
features: Python self.text and system.ui property and state helpers
local UI effects versus shared gateway data
prerequisites: Use the companion SparkStudio 0.2.0-preview.9 release or a newer compatible build with its bundled CPython runtime. Review and explicitly publish the project; the operator needs Operate permission for Python buttons.
The core exercise needs no tags, devices, database or internet connection. Designer Preview begins read-only; a gateway administrator must explicitly enable Live actions to run Python there.

The optional shared-title display intentionally reports unavailable until a String memory tag is configured at [default]Workshops/PythonUi/SharedTitle. The package creates no tags and contains no gateway-write action.
Follow the feature guide to add the optional shared tag-write button after gateway setup. That deliberate extension changes shared gateway data; all subscribed sessions see the shared title.
walkthrough: Import and explicitly publish the workshop. Open two operator tabs and confirm both start with the authored titles.
Press Rename this button. Its Python self.text assignment changes the clicked button to hi in this tab only; the result also reads self.text back. The second tab keeps the original button caption.
Edit New title in the first tab, then press Set sibling title or Set title via system.ui. Only that tab's unbound Local property title changes; the second tab retains its original title.
Press Set bound state title. Its Text binding follows the declared screen title state. Inspect the Python source and compare direct property assignments with state bindings.
Set a property title and private state in Station A. Confirm Station B remains unchanged. Repeat in Row 1 and verify Row 2 remains independent.
Refresh the operator tab to restore local authored defaults. Export the project and re-import it: transient state and property overrides are not saved.

Optionally follow the guide to create the shared String memory tag and add its Python write action. Set a shared title, then compare both operator tabs: the tag-bound display updates everywhere while local titles remain separate.

workshops.title: Component messaging workshop
workshops.summary: Send local browser messages from buttons and input events; compare private template and row delivery, screen broadcasts, popup sessions and receiver cleanup.
prerequisites: Use the companion SparkStudio 0.2.0-preview.9 release or a newer compatible build; older gateway-only messaging builds do not support this workshop.
Import into an isolated gateway, review and explicitly publish the project. Designer Preview starts with authored handlers blocked; enable Live actions to test there.
The workshop requires no Python, tags, device, database or internet connection. Session delivery stays inside one operator browser tab and its open popup.
walkthrough: Import and explicitly publish the workshop. Open the operator application; all receiver lines begin with waiting.
In Station A, press Send instance, then change Message text and commit it. Only Station A's Instance line changes. Repeat in Row 1 and verify Row 2 remains unchanged.
Toggle Send screen in any station. The main screen and all four station Screen lines change, while their Instance and Session lines retain their prior values.
Open the message popup and press Send popup screen. Only its Screen line changes. Press Send session from popup: the popup, main screen and all station Session lines change.
Compare a second operator browser tab: it receives no messages from the first. A message scope must exactly match a handler's configured scope.
Close the popup, choose Leave and test cleanup, and toggle Send session with no receivers. Confirm Accepted 0 handler(s). Return to fresh stations and confirm earlier messages are not replayed.

Choose Edit actions & events on a receiver in Designer and open Messages to inspect its declared state assignment. Inspect a native button's message type, scope and JSON payload in the same editor. Save, export and re-import to check the definitions remain editable.

workshops.title: Gateway events workshop
workshops.summary: Seven disabled Python event examples with explicit publication, schedules, tag observations, message echo and restart-surviving diagnostics.
features: tag value, quality and timestamp observers
run cancellation and durable bounded logs
prerequisites: Use the companion SparkStudio 0.2.0-preview.9 release or a newer compatible build implementing all seven gateway event types; preview.8 and earlier do not include this feature.
A gateway administrator and available CPython worker are required for execution and the published message tester. Every included script starts disabled and unpublished.
The optional tag-change exercise requires a separately configured memory tag at [default]Workshop/GatewayEvents/Counter. The package contains no gateway tags and its scripts do not write them.
Timer, lifecycle, message and schedule examples need no device, external database or internet connection. Exercise gateway stop/restart only on a disposable gateway.
walkthrough: Import the .sparkproj into an isolated gateway and open Scripting. Confirm seven gateway resources are present, disabled and not published; publish the read-only screen separately if desired.
Review Startup, Update and Timer, enable them, save and Publish scripts. Inspect activation and timer logs, then perform a resource save and inspect the update actor and resources.
Enable Workshop echo, save and publish, then send a JSON object through Test published handler. Confirm Result echoes it; unsaved edits disable this test.
Create the optional memory tag separately, enable the observer, then change the test tag and inspect initialChange, qualified values, changes and missedEvents.
Enable Scheduled and inspect its UTC next run. Compare fixed delay with fixed rate, which skips missed intervals instead of replaying a backlog.
On an isolated gateway, enable Shutdown and stop gracefully; restart and inspect retained run logs. Disable events and publish again when finished.

workshops.title: Scheduled backup workshop
workshops.summary: A read-only checkpoint for encrypted downloads, multiple SMB/FTP/FTPS/S3 destinations and schedules, independent age retention and isolated restore.
features: destination-specific SMB, FTP/FTPS and S3 forms
prerequisites: Use preview.11 or a later compatible build and an engineering administrator on a disposable gateway for multiple schedules and S3. Preview.10 has the earlier single-destination model.
Run tools/load-backup-example.mjs with SPARKSTUDIO_ADMIN_AUTH_FILE to create a new unpublished checkpoint project; --publish is an explicit option. The loader does not change gateway backup settings.
Choose an archive passphrase and dedicated writable test targets: SMB share, FTP/FTPS directory or S3 bucket/prefix. No credentials, remote folders or certificate material are included.

New schedules default to disabled, 02:00 in the gateway time zone and seven-day retention; destinations default to a 300-second transfer deadline. Save and verify each manual delivery before enabling its schedule.
Configuration archives exclude live databases, history and audit data. Keep separate database backups and use the offline full-backup procedure when complete stopped-gateway data is needed.
walkthrough: Load the checkpoint screen into the disposable gateway, review and publish SCHEDULE-LAB-A, then save an unpublished SCHEDULE-LAB-B draft.
Open Gateway Settings → Backups, save an archive passphrase with all schedules disabled, create a download and inspect its configuration scope.
In Destinations, configure two dedicated test targets with their own type-specific fields. Use an S3 bucket and prefix for the optional object-storage exercise.

In Schedules, add Nightly and Weekly copies referencing different targets, with separate weekdays, time zones and retention. Save both, run each manually and verify their results before enabling them.

Observe an unavailable-target failure without older-archive deletion. On a disposable gateway, use two schedules in one test folder to confirm the shorter retention does not prune the other schedule's archives.
Open Restore, restore to a fresh isolated directory, review quarantine and exclusions, and compare published A with draft B before permitting external activity.

workshops.title: Network HTTPS access
workshops.summary: A read-only published application for checking local management, generated or supplied HTTPS certificates, DNS or IPv4 identities and trusted operator access.
features: separate local management and network HTTPS ports
PEM certificate and exact DNS or iPAddress SAN validation
offline self-signed certificate generation and public trust export
prerequisites: Use preview.8 or later on a disposable gateway for generated certificates; preview.7 supports supplied certificates only.

Provide a DNS hostname or stable IPv4 address, then generate a certificate in setup or supply matching PEM files. Configure client trust and the intended firewall rule. IP access needs no DNS; generation needs no files or internet. No certificate material is distributed in this workshop.
Publish the supplied synthetic screen and grant a separate operator account View. No equipment, database, Python actions or external internet is required.
Run tools/load-network-example.mjs on a disposable local gateway with explicit administrator credentials to create its unpublished draft; the loader does not configure listeners.
walkthrough: Choose Network HTTPS with a distinct port and DNS hostname or specific IPv4 address. Select Generate a self-signed certificate (no files needed), or import a matching PEM pair.

For generated certificates, use administrator access on the gateway to copy only gateway-public.cer, verify its fingerprint and trust it on the operator computer following gateway-trust.txt. Before trust is configured a browser warning is expected.
Create the first administrator through local management, then import/review/publish this project and grant operator View.
Open the operator project from another computer using the trusted HTTPS hostname or IP address and inspect the local-only checkbox.

Inspect both actual listeners and certificate expiry, then verify a managed upgrade keeps the selected settings and certificate. Deliberate regeneration creates a replacement certificate that clients must trust again.

workshops.title: Gateway expressions and reviewed tag imports
workshops.summary: Synthetic counts and elapsed time drive a gateway-calculated rate and Boolean limit, with import preview and bad-quality exercises.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with expression tags and an engineering administrator account; public preview 5 predates this example.
The bundled Python runtime and operator Operate permission are needed for the synthetic Save action.
Use tools/load-tag-engineering-example.mjs with SPARKSTUDIO_ADMIN_AUTH_FILE, an unused project name and an unused [default]TagWorkshop namespace on a disposable gateway.
walkthrough: Load into an isolated gateway, inspect the tags, then publish and open the operator application.
Save 20 counts and 30 seconds: observe 40 per minute and a false limit; zero seconds propagates Bad_ExpressionError.
Disable Count and re-enable it. Preview an import, alter a tag, then observe stale-review rejection.

workshops.title: Gateway recovery lab
workshops.summary: Verify an offline encrypted full-gateway backup, isolated restore and explicit restart after review using synthetic data.
prerequisites: Use the companion gateway build with the --recovery CLI on a disposable data directory.
Stop all gateway and external file writers before backup. Keep the original directory and archive passphrase separately.
The lab screen makes no writes; the administrative walkthrough creates backup and restored files. Production gateways and live equipment are excluded.
walkthrough: Publish checkpoint A, then save an unpublished draft B and record synthetic gateway resources.
Stop, back up and inspect the archive. Restore into a new location and verify corrupted copies fail safely.
Start the restored copy on a separate local recovery port and verify connectors, Python and operator APIs are blocked.
Review synthetic destinations, approve and restart; compare the published and draft checkpoints and retained local resources.

workshops.title: Designer diagnostics
workshops.summary: Capture a bounded local snapshot of property failures, resource references, tag quality and retained browser-event messages.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with Project diagnostics and the built-in sample read-query provider.
No equipment, configured tags, external database, assets, Python or external network is required.
The optional deliberate browser-event failure needs administrator-enabled Live actions; default read-only Preview blocks authored scripts.
walkthrough: Enter Preview, set requested width to -1 and enable the invalid-color checkbox. Open Project diagnostics and inspect both Property bindings failures.
Filter for width, open its owner and verify Preview ends with that component selected without editing its definition.
Reenter Preview with valid defaults and refresh the snapshot. The former property errors disappear; Query properties explicitly reports its sample was not captured.
Try the deliberate event checkbox in read-only Preview and inspect the blocked event message. Optionally enable Live actions and repeat to see its authored failure and timestamp.
Inspect Resource references and Tag quality/connection. The example creates no tags; quality records reflect only the current gateway snapshot.

workshops.title: Canvas precision
workshops.summary: Select controls by type, match widths/heights with group-aware bounds and inspect authored grid coordinates.
prerequisites: Use the companion Designer build with Select type, Match size and numeric grid controls.
No tags, assets, scripts, database or external network is required.
walkthrough: Select Rectangle and match width, height and both dimensions; undo each operation.
Select Ellipse and compare the saved group with the independent circle. Match the grouped bounds and undo.
Use Ctrl+Shift+A or Cmd+Shift+A to select the chosen component type. Try grid 12 and then 0; drag while inspecting boundary guides and X/Y/W/H.
Save and publish an accepted arrangement. Runtime bindings remain authoritative over any authored coordinates they control.

workshops.title: Reusable visual styles
workshops.summary: Share appearance across screens and reusable forms while retaining local overrides and binding precedence.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with Visual styles in the Designer Project pane.
No equipment, tags, database, assets, scripts or external network is required.
walkthrough: Edit independent station notes in Preview and compare shared style appearance on both panels.
Change Section caption font size, cancel once, then Apply. The local 30-pixel override stays unchanged until cleared.
Toggle Use attention color: its binding wins while the assigned style still supplies font appearance. The disabled button remains disabled.
Change Station card background and compare Assembly with the Packing local override. Inspect why deleting a referenced style is blocked.
Undo the catalog once, then save and publish an accepted change. Export/re-import to verify stable style assignments.

workshops.title: Preview communication
workshops.summary: Start with gateway-enforced read-only Preview, then deliberately enable temporary draft actions as an administrator.
prerequisites: The built-in sample query needs no external database or configured tags.
The optional screen/template/popup Python message buttons require the bundled Python runtime and an administrator-enabled Live actions session.
Authored browser scripts are also disabled in default read-only Preview; publication has its own operator permission boundary.
walkthrough: Enter Preview and verify Live read-only, editable native local fields, pure bindings, sample query reads and popup navigation.
Try the three Python message buttons: each is blocked in read-only mode.
As a gateway administrator, open Enable live actions, cancel once, then confirm. The form resets and popup closes.
Run the optional screen, nested and popup message actions. They only return messages and do not write gateway data.
Return to read-only and verify the actions are blocked again. Exit and reopen Preview to confirm Live actions is never remembered.

workshops.title: Publication history
workshops.summary: Review and restore an earlier operator snapshot while preserving the current Designer draft.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with Publication history and a user with Publish permission.
No Python runtime, tags, assets, database or external network is required.
This is application snapshot history; separately published libraries/jobs, databases and gateway configuration are outside its restore scope.
walkthrough: Publish Release A, then edit the title to Release B and publish again. Compare the two history entries.
Leave Release C as a draft, review Release A and explicitly restore its operator publication.
Reload the operator application: Release A renders while the Designer retains Release C.
Use another Designer tab to publish while a restore review is open; the stale restore must be rejected.
Export and import the project. Its draft survives, while the new project starts unpublished without local publication history.

workshops.title: Offline caption translations
workshops.summary: Translate component captions through an offline message catalog while preserving live form values and parameter identities.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with Translations and the Preview/operator Language selector.
No database, equipment, tags, assets, scripts or external network is required.
This increment translates captions in en/es/fr/de/it/pt language families; number/date formatting, menu/option labels and RTL layout are separate work.
walkthrough: Enter distinct main and station notes in Preview. Select Spanish and verify captions change while notes, machine parameters and choice values remain unchanged.
Navigate using translated buttons. Select French and inspect the deliberately missing translation with its visible English fallback note.
Add the missing French translation, cancel once, then Apply. Undo restores the catalog in one step.
Inspect reference-protected message deletion and parameter-token validation. Save and explicitly publish an accepted translation.
Open an application-only operator link with ?lang=es. Export/re-import to verify the catalog and authored defaults.

workshops.title: Canvas authoring defaults
workshops.summary: Save starting document sizes and grid spacing without resizing existing screens and templates.
prerequisites: Use the companion build with Canvas authoring defaults in Project settings.
No tags, assets, scripts, database or external network is required.
walkthrough: Inspect the existing 1100 × 680 screen and 300 × 160 template. Their dimensions remain independent of project defaults.
Add a screen and template to inspect the configured 1400 × 900 and 700 × 450 starting sizes; undo each creation.
Edit defaults in Project settings, cancel once, then apply a valid change and undo it.
Save grid 12, change the session toolbar grid to 4, then reopen Designer and verify the saved initial grid returns.
Export/re-import and repeat the new-document checks. Existing geometry stays unchanged.

workshops.title: Gateway operations
workshops.summary: Explore the administrator resource/session console and bounded operational diagnostics using a synthetic application.
features: deployment configuration provenance and observed transport
prerequisites: Use preview.11 or a later compatible build and a gateway administrator for the current Gateway Settings panels and automatic observations.
The project itself needs no tags, assets, database, scripts or external network.
Use only a disposable sign-in for the optional session revocation exercise; it changes that session’s authentication state.
walkthrough: Import and publish the named workshop. Locate its Designer/operator links in Projects, then open Gateway Settings to inspect resource counts.
Compare engineering and operator sessions. If testing revocation, identify and revoke only a disposable session, leaving the current and other sessions active.
Open Diagnostics and compare automatic observations approximately 15 seconds apart. Inspect CPU, memory, disk and bounded route records.
Verify the observation timestamp advances while visible without a Refresh button. Failed observations retain the last data with a warning and contextual Retry.

Open Deployment. Compare actual listeners, startup values and saved settings. Edit a loopback HTTP port, Validate draft, then Cancel changes. Verify the latest saved revision is retrieved and actual listeners remain unchanged. Saving/restart/recovery requires the separate disposable-gateway exercise in the guide.
Download and inspect the local support snapshot; it excludes credentials, identities, authored project content and tag values. Ordinary Designer/operator users cannot open the console.

workshops.title: Asset library and replacements
workshops.summary: Review structured image use and preview selective replacements across screens and shared template definitions.
prerequisites: Load the authored fixture into a separate project and bring two local PNG, JPEG or WebP images, each up to 512 KiB.
Upload both images and assign image A to Desk photo, Detail photo and the shared template image before publication. The fixture intentionally contains no image files.
After setup, normal project export produces a portable .sparkproj with the referenced image assets. No tags, database or scripts are required.
walkthrough: Upload two local images, configure the three authored image references and open Asset library.
Search by image name or shared template location and open a listed owning component without editing it.
Preview replacement with image B; select only Desk photo, apply and use one Undo. Other references remain on A.
Replace only the shared template image and compare both placements, then undo.
Save all replacements while the operator stays on its previous publication. Publish explicitly, export and re-import the configured project.

workshops.title: Bulk replacement

workshops.title: Industrial device connections
workshops.summary: Configure isolated Modbus TCP, six EtherNet/IP controller families, Siemens S7 and Beckhoff ADS points, then read and review synthetic scalar commands.
features: ControlLogix, CompactLogix, Micro800, MicroLogix, SLC 500 and PLC-5 address/type profiles
Saved point maps and qualified native symbol mapping
Reviewed scalar writes and physical alias serialization
prerequisites: Requires 0.2.0-preview.12 or a later compatible release containing the four industrial drivers and six EtherNet/IP family profiles; preview.11 and earlier do not contain these drivers. Exact artifact/source evidence is recorded separately in docs/architecture/PARITY.md. EtherNet/IP dependencies remain pinned to libplctag 1.5.2 / NativeImport 1.0.41, native core 2.6.0.

Use isolated simulators or lab PLCs with independently created synthetic Int16 storage. Logix and Micro800 use SyntheticSetpoint INT; MicroLogix, SLC 500 and PLC-5 use an allocated N7:0 integer element. Logix requires its numeric route; the other four use blank direct routes. Only ControlLogix/CompactLogix have native catalogs. ControlLogix/CompactLogix String is rejected until controller structure-schema qualification is implemented; Micro800 String and DH+ routes are also excluded. PCCC ST strings retain their bounded file profile.

ADS uses an existing router or a shared gateway-managed router when TCP 48898 has no listener. Its local AMS identity must match, existing routers need a target route, and the controller always needs a back-route. S7 requires accessible non-optimized DB layouts.

Run tools/load-industrial-devices-example.mjs on an isolated gateway to create only its unpublished project, then configure connections/tags separately and explicitly publish. Rebind the one EtherNet/IP Setpoint tag deliberately to exercise each available family.
Operators need Commands and tag-read scope for [default]IndustrialWorkshop/. Operate alone cannot write. Physical device/firmware qualification remains separate for every family.
walkthrough: Load the authored draft; confirm all unconfigured values remain unavailable.
Create a protocol-specific lab connection and saved Setpoint map entry. Choose the actual EtherNet/IP family, route and Int16 lab address from the guide; save its map before testing Micro800/PCCC.
Browse/read without writing and add the device tag. Publish explicitly, review 25, cancel, then review and confirm; verify one write and matching fresh readback.
Try 101 and an Operate-only account to verify rejection before dispatch. Change lab state or disable the connection after review and verify the old intent is rejected.

Repeat with each available protocol and EtherNet/IP family. Rebind its Setpoint tag explicitly between connections, recording controller/firmware/OS/dependency evidence rather than transferring acceptance between families.
Inspect bad quality and command uncertainty after lab disconnect, then remove/rebind saved device tags and UDT members before deleting the connection.
